prompt: The robot prints around a bare line. What appears on the screen, in order?

options.text: `GO` then `STOP` then `DONE`. The bare 8 is quiet and the prints carry on.
options.feedback: Right. The bare 8 is valid but quiet; the prints before and after it each add their line.

options.text: `GO` then `8` then `STOP` then `DONE`. The bare 8 shows itself between them.
options.feedback: A bare value writes no screen line, in any position. Only print adds lines.

options.text: `GO`. The bare 8 stops the program, so STOP and DONE never print.
options.feedback: A bare value is valid code, not an error. The program runs on: STOP and DONE print.

options.text: `GO` then `STOP` then `DONE`. A bare value shows itself only when last.
options.feedback: Add a last line 8 after DONE: the screen still shows only GO, STOP and DONE — bare values never write lines in a complete program.
options.partial_reason: Right: GO, STOP, DONE. Wrong: that a last bare value displays itself; in a complete program no bare value writes a screen line.

explanation: The bare 8 is valid code but quiet wherever it sits. The prints around it each add a line: GO, then STOP, then DONE.
